construction_markdown:
Let
\[
p(Z)=Z^{16}+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1,
\qquad F=\mathbb F_2[Z]/(p),
\]
and let \(\alpha=Z\bmod p\). Write each \(z\in F\) uniquely as \(z=\sum_{i=0}^{15}z_i\alpha^i\).

Fix
\[
A=\left\{\sum_{i=0}^{14}u_i\alpha^i:u_i\in\mathbb F_2\right\},
\qquad V=\mathbb F_2^{15}.
\]
Both sets have \(2^{15}=32768\) elements. Order them by their binary coefficient integers.

Define the binary inner encoder
\[
H(z)=\left(z_0+\sum_{i=1}^{15}z_i y_i\right)_{y\in V}.
\]
This identifies the additive space of \(F\) with \(\operatorname{RM}(1,15)\).

For every polynomial
\[
f(X)=\sum_{j=0}^{64}c_jX^j\in F[X],
\]
define
\[
C(f)=\bigl(H(f(a))_y\bigr)_{(a,y)\in A\times V},
\]
with outer blocks ordered by \(a\), then inner coordinates by \(y\). Set
\[
C=\{C(f):\deg f\le64\}\subseteq\mathbb F_2^{2^{30}}.
\]
Equivalently, this concatenates the Reed–Solomon code \([32768,65,32704]_{2^{16}}\) with \(\operatorname{RM}(1,15)=[32768,16,16384]_2\).

discussion_posts.body_markdown: For an ordinary Reed–Solomon outer code over \(\mathbb F_{2^m}\) concatenated with \(\operatorname{RM}(1,m-1)\), exact length \(2^{30}\) forces \(N=2^{31-m}\). Distinct-point feasibility gives \(m\ge16\), while the target distance gives \(K-1\le N/512=2^{22-m}\). Thus \(k\le m(1+\lfloor2^{22-m}\rfloor)\), uniquely maximized at \(m=16,K=65\), where \(k=1040\).

discussion_posts.body_markdown: The full degree-65 extension fails. For any 65-point \(R\subset A\), let \(g=\prod_{r\in R}(X-r)\). Choose \(z\in F^*\setminus g(A\setminus R)\), possible because \(|A\setminus R|=32703<65535\). Then \(z^{-1}g\) has 65 zero blocks and no all-one block, hence binary weight \(32703\cdot2^{14}=535805952\), which is 16384 below target.
discussion_posts.subject: Why outer dimension 66 fails

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Let \(D_0\subset F^A\) be the degree-at-most-64 evaluation code. Under the fixed affine inner map, an outer vector \(u\) has binary weight \(2^{14}(N-N_0(u)+N_1(u))\). Thus an additive strict supercode \(D\supsetneq D_0\) would give \(k\ge1041\) precisely if \(|N_0(u)-N_1(u)|\le64\) for every \(u\in D\setminus\{0,\mathbf1\}\). Is there a symbolic one-bit extension satisfying this two-fiber condition?
discussion_posts.subject: Can an additive outer extension reach 1041?

distance_audit: Every nonzero outer polynomial of degree at most 64 has at most 64 roots among the 32768 distinct points of A, hence at least 32704 nonzero outer symbols.
Every nonzero inner affine word has weight at least 2^14=16384; the symbol 1 gives the all-one word of weight 2^15.
Therefore every nonzero concatenated word has weight at least 32704·16384=(2^15−2^6)2^14=2^29−2^20=535822336.

For equality, take the lexicographically first 64-point set R⊂A, g(X)=∏_{r∈R}(X−r), and the lexicographically first z∈F* outside g(A\R). Then z^−1g has exactly 64 zero evaluations and never evaluates to 1 elsewhere. Its remaining inner blocks are all nonconstant and have weight exactly 2^14.
explicitness_audit: The field is fixed by the displayed degree-16 polynomial. Repeated squaring gives Z^(2^8)≡Z^8+Z^7+Z^3+Z and Z^(2^16)≡Z modulo p; Euclidean division of p by Z^8+Z^7+Z^3 has successive nonzero remainders Z^2+1 and 1. Rabin's degree-16 criterion therefore proves p irreducible.
The polynomial basis, the 32768-element evaluation set A, the inner domain V, and both coordinate orderings are specified.
The outer message consists of exactly 65 unrestricted F-coefficients. No divisor, shortening, puncturing, padding, repetition, sampled object, or random choice is hidden.
The scaling element used to certify exact distance is the first element outside an explicitly defined finite image, so the witness is symbolically recoverable.

proof_markdown:
## Theorem

There is a deterministic binary linear code with exact parameters
\[
[2^{30},1040,535{,}822{,}336]_2.
\]
Its rate is \(1040/2^{30}=65/2^{26}\). The submission remains under review pending independent acceptance.

## Field certificate

Let
\[
p(Z)=Z^{16}+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1.
\]
Repeated squaring modulo \(p\) gives
\[
Z^{2^8}\equiv Z^8+Z^7+Z^3+Z,
\qquad Z^{2^{16}}\equiv Z.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\gcd(p,Z^{2^8}+Z)=\gcd(p,Z^8+Z^7+Z^3)=1,
\]
because the Euclidean algorithm has successive nonzero remainders \(Z^2+1\) and \(1\). Since 2 is the only prime divisor of 16, the finite-field irreducibility criterion proves that \(p\) is irreducible. Hence the displayed quotient is a fixed field \(F\) of order \(2^{16}\).

## Linearity, length, and dimension

The map \(H:F\to\mathbb F_2^{2^{15}}\) is \(\mathbb F_2\)-linear. It is injective: evaluation at \(y=0\) recovers \(z_0\), and comparison with the values at the fifteen unit vectors recovers \(z_1,\ldots,z_{15}\).

The space of polynomials of degree at most 64 has dimension 65 over \(F\), hence binary dimension \(65\cdot16=1040\). If its concatenated word is zero, injectivity of \(H\) implies that \(f(a)=0\) for every \(a\in A\). This gives 32768 roots to a polynomial of degree at most 64, so \(f=0\). Thus the composite encoder is injective and \(C\) has dimension exactly 1040.

There are \(|A|=2^{15}\) outer blocks and each block has \(|V|=2^{15}\) coordinates. Therefore
\[
|A||V|=2^{30}=1{,}073{,}741{,}824.
\]
All maps used are additive, so \(C\) is binary linear.

## Minimum distance

Let \(f\ne0\). It has at most 64 roots in \(A\), so at least
\[
32768-64=32704
\]
of its outer symbols are nonzero. If \(z\in F\setminus\{0,1\}\), the affine function defining \(H(z)\) has a nonzero linear part and hence exactly \(2^{14}\) ones. The symbol \(1\) produces the all-one block of weight \(2^{15}\). Thus every nonzero outer symbol contributes at least \(2^{14}\), and
\[
\operatorname{wt}(C(f))\ge32704\cdot2^{14}
=(2^{15}-2^6)2^{14}
=2^{29}-2^{20}
=535{,}822{,}336.
\]
This covers every nonzero codeword.

The bound is attained. Let \(R\) be the first 64 elements of \(A\) and put
\[
g(X)=\prod_{r\in R}(X-r).
\]
The image \(g(A\setminus R)\) has at most 32704 elements, fewer than the 65535 elements of \(F^*\). Let \(z\) be the first nonzero field element outside this image and set \(f=z^{-1}g\). Then \(f\) vanishes precisely at the 64 points of \(R\), and \(f(a)\ne1\) for every \(a\notin R\). Consequently its remaining 32704 inner blocks are nonconstant affine words, each of weight exactly \(2^{14}\). Hence
\[
d_{\min}(C)=535{,}822{,}336.
\]

## Exact optimization inside the RS–affine-inner family

For an outer Reed–Solomon code over \(\mathbb F_{2^m}\) concatenated with \(\operatorname{RM}(1,m-1)\), exact final length forces
\[
N2^{m-1}=2^{30},\qquad N=2^{31-m}.
\]
Distinct-point Reed–Solomon evaluation requires \(N\le2^m\), hence \(m\ge16\). If the outer dimension is \(K\), its distance is \(N-K+1\). The target condition becomes
\[
(N-K+1)2^{m-2}
\ge N2^{m-2}-N2^{m-11},
\]
so
\[
K-1\le N/512=2^{22-m}.
\]
Therefore
\[
k\le m\bigl(1+\lfloor2^{22-m}\rfloor\bigr).
\]
At \(m=16\), this is \(16(64+1)=1040\), achieved above. At \(m=17\) it is 561; it decreases through \(m=22\), and for \(m\ge23\) it is at most \(m\le31\). Thus \(m=16,K=65\) is the unique optimum in this concrete algebraic family.
